reasons: Status is correctly characterized as missing: the cited paragraphs and the finding's document-wide check show Article XVI contains indemnification and recall provisions but no coverage covenant, and no insurance obligation appears elsewhere, which sits below the fallback (E&O 1M / cyber 2M) for a counterparty conducting Clinical Studies and manufacturing/supplying Product.

Redline is directionally correct for our side (Ono as licensee/customer): it imposes the obligation on Array (counterparty/Licensor) and does not create any reciprocal burden on us; offering mutuality is left to negotiation in the comment.

Edit is a pure insertion of a single new Section 16.7 appended after the last paragraph of Article XVI (indemnification/recalls) with no alteration of existing text — the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position, and placement is sensible given the rule's guidance to add a short paragraph in the general/indemnity area.

Inserted limits track the preferred position (CGL 1M/2M, professional/product-and-clinical-trial liability 2M, cyber 5M where our data is handled, statutory workers' comp, certificates on request), with a context-appropriate substitution of product/clinical-trial liability for E&O in a pharma development deal; the self-insurance option is a reasonable commercial softener rather than a material weakening.

Comment is accurate and on-tone: it correctly notes the absence of insurance backing Array's Section 16.2 indemnities (including Products Liability Claims and clinical trial injury), states what was added, and offers the playbook fallback (product liability 1M / cyber 2M) and mutuality; prefix and first-person-plural style are correct.

Deterministic checks both pass (operation applies; insurance obligation present), consistent with the substantive review; only residual risk is section numbering if an existing 16.7 exists, which is a formatting matter easily reconciled and not a substantive defect.
